newsitem.title: USA: Quantech says Shaw resigns as pres, CEO.
newsitem.headline: Quantech says Shaw resigns as pres, CEO.

text.p: Quantech Ltd said Thursday R.H. Joseph Shaw resigned as chairman, president and chief executive, and board member Robert Case was named interim chief executive.
Quantech also said it named James Lyons, a private investor and a Quantech director, as chairman. Shaw will remain a director and serve as a consultant to the company.
In addition, the medical products company said it received gross proceeds of $1.1 million from a private placement of promissory notes and warrants to purchase common stock.

The company said Shaw agreed to step aside to make room for an executive with experience in operating a commercial diagnostics company. A search has been launched for a permanent replacement for Shaw.
"We appreciate his efforts, and we are gratified that he has agreed to support the company as it continues work to commercialize the product," Case said in a statement.

"However, as we move toward our FDA submission, the Board and Mr. Shaw agreed that, for the company to make the transition from its entrepreneurial roots, it needed a chief executive with a strong background in operating a commercial diagnostics company," Case said. "We have launched a search to find the right individual to lead the company and facilitate additional financing and, or, a strategic partnership."
Proceeds of the offering will be used for development of Quantech's diagnostic system and preparation of a 510(k) application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for marketing of the system.
Quantech also said it has settled a lawsuit against the former manufacturer of a component part of its diagnostic system. Terms of the settlement were not disclosed.
